severity_scale.P0: Critical required-use usability, trust or delivery failure
severity_scale.P2: Worthwhile improvement or conditional maintenance gap

findings.title: The small icon is a reduction of an illustration, not a reliable distinctive micro-mark
findings.release_scope: Primary symbol / favicon launch; not a repository-only hero blocker
findings.condition: 16, 24 and 32 CSS pixels, light/dark surroundings; DPR 1 and 2

evidence.detail: Favicon PNGs are exact decoded-pixel matches of Lanczos reductions; ICO frames equal those PNGs.
Bright-content proxy in 1254-square source occupies approximately 11.05 x 8.74 pixels when scaled to 16; this is not a semantic silhouette measurement.
Play/window remain; puzzle detail loses identity at 16 and remains weak at 24/32.

findings.confidence: High on detail loss; medium on unfamiliar-user recognition
findings.observation: The plugin cue becomes a small bright patch while frame/play and sparkle dominate.
findings.interpretation: The retained details identify a media-player category better than this catalog.
findings.consequence: A tab/avatar can be technically visible yet weakly identifiable.
findings.correction: Design a bounded optical small-size family from a chosen invariant cue; increase useful occupied area and remove details that cannot survive.
acceptance_tests: Inspect exported 16/24/32 CSS sizes at 100% and DPR 1/2, separately recording source pixels.
A distinctive non-letter cue must remain identifiable without sparkle or color alone.
Compare before/after under identical backgrounds; run small human matching/confusion review before approving the primary symbol.

findings.title: The primary visual proposition is a player with plugins rather than an independent catalog
findings.release_scope: Public positioning; primary identity approval; mitigable for repository-only release
findings.condition: Standalone symbols and reduced public compositions

evidence.detail: Play triangle, application window, traffic-light dots, puzzle panel and sparkle recur. Full-size social text does say curated catalog, but no public composition explicitly says independent/community.
Official IINA uses dark rounded-square/cyan play/purple bars; mpv a purple circular play mark; Awesome uses pink sunglasses and a wordmark.
Possible app/official-product interpretation. Not evidence of actual user confusion, copying, infringement or AI-product identity.

findings.observation: The art prominently depicts a media application and extensions.
findings.interpretation: Context is relevant, but it overstates playback and understates curation/discovery.
findings.consequence: The intended independent-community role may disappear when descriptive text is unreadable.
findings.correction: Add an explicit independent-community descriptor; choose a primary silhouette distinguishable from an app-window/play icon. Keep player art as secondary illustration.
acceptance_tests: Approve exact role copy against current project brief.
Full card/README context must identify the project as an independent catalog, not an official store/player.
Review actual IINA/mpv/Awesome references side by side; seek human first impressions, not a legal originality certificate.

findings.title: Supporting raster copy loses utility at plausible small presentation widths
findings.release_scope: Social-card release; README only if required meaning depends on image text

evidence.detail: Threshold-detected ink spans: social descriptor 23px/1280 => 5.75 CSS px at 320; category line 15 => 3.75; hero descriptor 24px/1800 => 5.2 at 390. These are glyph-ink spans, not font sizes.
Name remains readable; category row and long descriptor cease to be reliable reading content.
Mobile-width hero title remains, descriptor is too small to carry required meaning.

findings.confidence: High for geometry and reviewer legibility judgment
findings.observation: The longest explanatory text is also the smallest content.
findings.interpretation: More source pixels do not enlarge CSS-presented words.
findings.consequence: The explanation needed to correct player-first positioning is the first element lost.
findings.correction: Use a shorter, larger role line on the social card; remove the tiny category inventory or move it to live text. Keep README meaning outside the illustration.
acceptance_tests: Read name plus role line without zoom at the agreed minimum social presentation; 320x160 is the proposed stress test.
At a 390-pixel README column and with the image disabled, the live title and complete independent-catalog description remain available.
Check visual hierarchy and ordinary-text contrast in actual integration; do not treat logotype exemption as a whole-banner exemption.

findings.title: Website example is not a complete deployed Open Graph integration
findings.condition: Example head lines 10-17 and deployed route resolution

evidence.detail: Example includes title, description, image placeholder, image dimensions and alt; no og:type or og:url.
Open Graph defines title/type/image/url as four basic required properties.
No actual site, absolute public URL, route fetch or social unfurl is supplied/tested.

findings.confidence: High for snippet; not assessed for any unseen site
findings.observation: The example intentionally contains placeholders and is missing two basic OG properties.
findings.interpretation: This is an incomplete example, not evidence that a published site is broken.
findings.consequence: Copying it unchanged can produce incomplete metadata and unresolved image/icon references.
findings.correction: Supply canonical URL/type, resolve placeholders/base path, and match image dimensions to whichever export is actually served.
acceptance_tests: Rendered head contains title/type/image/url with no unresolved placeholder.
All served icon/manifest/image URLs return appropriate resources and dimensions.
Verify actual GitHub setting separately from website metadata; test selected browsers/platforms only once a deployment exists.

findings.title: Brand art and typography are not available as editable production masters
findings.release_scope: Ongoing maintenance; a dependency of any approved redesign, not a one-off upload blocker
findings.condition: Future text/layout/shape edits and new exports

evidence.detail: Four RGB artwork originals; no layered brand source, text-layout source or font binaries. Banner text is rasterized.
An SVG inside credential metadata is a generator icon, not vector construction of Awesome IINA artwork.

findings.observation: The exporter can resize artwork but cannot edit the baked-in headline, descriptor or icon geometry.
findings.interpretation: Repeatable resizing is not an editable identity system.
findings.consequence: Every meaningful correction needs reconstruction or regeneration without a stable design master.
findings.correction: Create an editable compact-symbol source and card layout with live editable text. Preserve complex hero illustration as raster where appropriate; record chosen font and license.
acceptance_tests: Change descriptor text and regenerate without repainting underlying glyph pixels.
Inspect brand vector source for actual editable paths, not a whole-image raster wrapper.
Record licensed font dependency without redistributing font binaries in this audit.
Keep original hashes and map each revised export to its new source.

findings.title: The only background treatment is an opaque dark canvas
findings.release_scope: Inline brand placement or neutral-background reuse, only when selected
findings.condition: White/light surroundings and proposed single-color use

evidence.detail: All 23 images/containers are fully opaque. ICO alpha is 255 throughout. No transparent or genuine one-color brand variant.
Grayscale keeps geometry, but an alpha-only mask is a solid rectangle; light surroundings expose a dark rectangular tile.

findings.observation: A dark rectangular backing is part of every icon asset.
findings.interpretation: This can be an intentional tile, but not a transparent universal-placement logo.
findings.consequence: Inline use can look boxed; a mask or knockout cannot be inferred from existing alpha.
findings.correction: Document dark-tile use as intentional. Add an actual cutout/light-background variant only for a confirmed placement; design one-color artwork only for a confirmed use.
acceptance_tests: Inspect any new transparency with measured zero/partial alpha and on light/dark checkerboards.
No matte halo or disappearing silhouette at approved display sizes.
Do not add maskable purpose or claim monochrome support merely by changing metadata.

findings.title: Reuse governance and credential-preservation policy are unresolved
findings.release_scope: Public asset reuse; escalate only if release asserts rights/verified credentials not established
findings.condition: Source provenance, derivative metadata and public reuse claims

evidence.detail: All four originals contain caBX metadata with claimed gpt-image 2.0 creation and OpenAI Media Service API generator; allActionsIncluded=false. Four declared data hashes independently match; signature/trust/timestamp validation not performed.
Derivative PNGs have IHDR/IDAT/IEND only; no caBX. Source originals remain preserved.
Provenance docs acknowledge no approved standard or determined third-party licensing; no asset reuse license provided.
Content binding, signature verification and trust evaluation are different validation steps.

findings.confidence: High for presence/absence and parsed fields; unverified authorship/rights
findings.observation: The kit has more embedded provenance than its overview explains, but neither the signatures nor rights were established here.
findings.interpretation: Preserved credentials and hashes are useful evidence, not a license or originality certificate.
findings.consequence: Maintainers could overstate provenance or public reuse permissions; metadata loss in resized copies is undocumented in detail.
findings.correction: Record parsed credential scope/status and omitted derivative metadata; retain original credentials untouched. Record maintainer authorization and explicit asset reuse terms. Use a proper validator only if making a verified-credential claim.
acceptance_tests: Document which metadata persists in originals and which does not survive exports.
Never transplant an original signature onto altered pixels.
Maintainer approves selected assets and states reuse policy without claiming legal clearance.
Any verified-C2PA claim is accompanied by an actual validator report with trust/signature/time scope.

findings.title: Color space and exact palette roles are not established
findings.release_scope: Cross-tool export maintenance and color-critical reuse
findings.condition: Source interpretation and future output conversion

evidence.detail: No ICC/sRGB/gAMA/cHRM/cICP color declaration found in any PNG.
Representative text-core/background ratios are 12.88,16.43,18.44 under explicit sRGB assumption; not whole-text minimum or display calibration.
Major frame/play geometry remains in Chromium color-vision simulations; small-detail loss persists.

findings.confidence: High for metadata; medium for color consistency risk
findings.observation: RGB values exist but source encoding and reusable palette tokens are undocumented.
findings.interpretation: The images are not demonstrated color-broken, but color-critical reproduction is not established.
findings.consequence: Future tools may choose inconsistent interpretation or undocumented accent colors.
findings.correction: Select and document the intended output color space after visual confirmation; define named color roles from approved source samples or explicitly proposed colors.
acceptance_tests: Record color-space assignment/conversion, tool version and approved before/after visual comparison.
Do not label an existing unknown source profile as measured sRGB.
Retest ordinary supporting text contrast and grayscale recognition in revised assets.
